summary: Texture format auto-detection and decoding dispatcher. Tries seven image decoders in a fixed priority order (BMP, TGA/generic, DDS-header, unknown sub_50210E, DDS-surface, PPM, DDS-validate) on the raw buffer a2/a3, recording the active candidate in the object at this+0x44/this+0x48 and the caller payload at this+0x40. On the first candidate whose decoder returns a non-negative status it stops; on failure it frees buffers and surface nodes owned by this, resets ownership flags, and retries the next candidate. After success it optionally fills an output descriptor a4 (width/height/depth/FourCC/format/surface-count from this+0xC..this+0x48) and finalizes the linked surface list rooted at this+0x4C/this+0x50. Returns 0 on success, -2005529767 when all candidates fail.

Each iteration records the caller payload a5 at this+0x40, the candidate index at this+0x48, and the constant format code 3 at this+0x44.

Store the selected decoder's return value as the candidate status v5.
If the candidate status v5 is >= 0, the decode succeeded and the retry loop is exited.
On failure, if the buffer-1 pointer this+0x4 and its ownership flag this+0x38 are both set, free buffer 1 via FreeWrapper_7bcf; likewise free buffer 2 when this+0x8 and this+0x3C are set.
On failure, release the surface head node this+0x4C and the next-surface pointer this+0x50 via ShortComputation_0fae(node, 1) when each is non-null.
Reset decoder state for the next candidate: zero this+0x4, this+0x8, this+0x38, this+0x3C, this+0x4C and this+0x50, then increment the candidate counter v22.
If all seven candidates failed (v22 == 7), return -2005529767.
If the output descriptor a4 is non-null, populate it from the decoded object.
Derive the output FourCC code from this+0x0 via FourCCDecoder.

Zero the 0x1C-byte output descriptor a4, then fill width from this+0xC, height from this+0x10, depth from this+0x14, base surface count 1, format from this+0x44 and the candidate index from this+0x48.
Count the surfaces in the linked list rooted at this+0x4C by walking each node's next pointer (node+0x4C) and incrementing the surface count a4[3].

Finalize each surface node in the chain: copy node+0xC to node+0x20 and node+0x10 to node+0x24, save node+0x14 into node+0x2C, zero node+0x18, node+0x1C and node+0x28, then advance through node+0x4C and to the next surface at this+0x50.
Return 0 after successful decode and surface finalization.
